title: A practice built around *the length of an appointment.*
intro: Aurevia is a small medical practice in a Georgian house in Marylebone: physicians who look after people over years, consultants who work alongside them, and a team whose job is to make the whole thing feel unhurried.
hero_alt: The first-floor waiting room: low sofas, a timber table and tall windows onto the garden

story.headline: Why it *exists.*
paragraphs: Aurevia was set up by physicians who had spent their careers in hospitals and busy practices, and who kept noticing the same thing: most of what went wrong for patients was not a lack of technology. It was a lack of time in the room, and a lack of anyone holding the whole picture.

So the practice is arranged around those two problems. First appointments last an hour. Every patient has a named physician who reads every letter, and the specialists are in the same building, sharing one record and a lunch table. None of this is complicated. It is simply rarer than it should be.

principles.title: Time before tests
principles.detail: A proper history usually tells us more than a scan. We take the time first, then choose the tests that will actually change a decision.

principles.title: One physician, one record
principles.detail: Your physician is the person every specialist reports back to. You never have to be the messenger between your own doctors.

principles.title: Fees before treatment
principles.detail: Every fee is published, and anything beyond the published list is quoted in writing before it is arranged.

principles.title: Plain English, in writing
principles.detail: After any assessment or consultation you receive a letter that explains what we found and why we suggest what we do.

not_doing: Sell whole-body scans to people without symptoms
Run an emergency department. For emergencies, call 999
Share your records with an employer or insurer without your written consent
Pay or receive commission for referrals, supplements or products
Book anything before you have agreed the fee

team.name: Leila Moradi
team.note: Usually the first voice you hear. Leila routes enquiries, books appointments and chases results so you don't have to.

team.name: Samuel Okoye
team.note: Looks after members and organisation programmes, including travel-heavy calendars and Saturday clinics.

team.name: Hannah Pryce
team.note: Runs phlebotomy, ECGs and the assessment mornings, and knows exactly how to find a difficult vein.

team.name: Irene Kovač
team.note: Responsible for the house, the rota and the standards behind them. Also the person to write to if something wasn't right.

partners.gp: If you have an NHS GP, we recommend keeping them. With your permission, we send them a copy of every letter so both records stay complete, and we will say plainly when something is better continued on the NHS.
partners.insurers: Most UK private medical insurers recognise our consultants for specialist and diagnostic care. Call your insurer before your first appointment for an authorisation code; we will tell you exactly what to ask for, and bill them directly.
